title: Bitterness & Forgiveness: A Biblical Perspective
description: Chapter 4 summary and homework from Marriage Enrichment 2022

gospel_data.title: Bitterness & Forgiveness: A Biblical Perspective

nestedSubsections.title: Bitterness defined
nestedSubsections.content:
1. Bitterness is defined as being, “cold, harsh, stern, cruel.” It is “characterized by intense animosity.”

  2. When a person has a spirit of animosity towards another person it means they have a “hostile spirit” or a “feeling of ill-will” towards that person, and they tend to display this hostility in their actions.

  3. A bitter person harbors a spirit of animosity toward the one they are embittered against.
    Colossians 3:19 Husbands, love your wives and do not be embittered against them.

nestedSubsections.title: General symptoms of Bitterness:
nestedSubsections.content:
1. A history of tones and words that are harsh and sharp.

  2. A history of actions taken against one’s spouse.

  3. It will have reached a state that is ongoing.1

nestedSubsections.title: The primary cause of bitterness:
nestedSubsections.content:
1. Martha Peace states, “Bitterness grows when you take into account a wrong suffered.”2
    1 Corinthians 7:28 But if you do marry, you have not sinned; and if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. But those who marry will face many troubles in this life, and I want to spare you this. (NIV)

  2. Bitterness occurs when there is an unforgiven sin between a couple.

nestedSubsections.title: Specific Signs of Bitterness:
nestedSubsections.content:
Hebrews 12:15 See to it that no one comes short of the grace of God; that no root of bitterness springing up causes trouble, and by it may be defiled.

  1. Gossip & Slander

    1. Gossip is “the spreading of unfavorable information about someone else, even if that information is true.”3

    2. Slander is “making a false statement or misrepresentation about another person that defames or damages the person’s reputation.”4

    3. Gossip and slander are both sins of the tongue. The bitter person develops such anger and resentment in their heart that it becomes difficult to restrain the tongue.
      Luke 6:45 The good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings forth what is good; and the evil man out of the evil treasure brings forth what is evil; for his mouth speaks from that which fills his heart.

  2. Ungratefulness or Complaining

    1. Complaining and a lack of gratitude go hand in hand.
      Philippians 2:14 Do all things without grumbling or disputing,

  3. Harshly Judging a Person’s Motives

    1. A person who is bitter eventually holds feelings of animosity towards the individual they are embittered against. Because of this, it becomes difficult to see anything good about that person or their motives.

      1. Martha Peace states that the embittered wife might say, “He only did that to look good to his parents.”5

      2. She also states, “Your husband will be unable to do anything right in your eyes even if he is trying.”6

  4. Victim Mentality

    1. An embittered person will often focus on how they have been hurt, on their “rightness” and blame the other person for all that is wrong in the relationship.

  5. Excessive Sorrow

    1. Once records of wrongs suffered have been stored up over time, they begin crowding out joy and happiness, leaving only continuous depression and sorrow.

  6. Vengeful Spirit
    Ephesians 4:26 Be angry, and yet do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger.

    1. When outward forms of revenge begin manifesting, a marriage is in serious trouble.

    2. If a marriage has reached a state where couples are punishing each other, the unhappiness and loneliness can become so acute that their marriage is in danger of infidelity or divorce.

  7. Brooding

    1. To brood is “to meditate with morbid persistence.”7 It is to repeatedly dwell on hurts and wrongs suffered.
      1 Corinthians 13:5 It does not act unbecomingly; it does not seek its own, is not provoked, does not take into account a wrong suffered.

  8. Loss of Joy

    1. A loss of joy between spouses will spread to a loss of joy in the Lord, if not dealt with.

    2. Martha Peace states, “The wife has little or no delight in her relationship with the Lord. Because of her sin, instead of God’s peace and joy, she is experiencing intense emotional pain and misery.”8

  9. Critical Judgmental Attitude

    1. A person that has become bitter will be critical and judgmental toward the one they are bitter against.
      Matthew 7:5 You hypocrite, first take the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother’s eye.

nestedSubsections.title: Bitterness is a Sin of the Heart:
nestedSubsections.content:
Luke 6:43-45 For there is no good tree which produces bad fruit, nor, on the other hand, a bad tree which produces good fruit. For each tree is known by its own fruit. For men do not gather figs from thorns, nor do they pick grapes from a briar bush. The good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings forth what is good; and the evil man out of the evil treasure brings forth what is evil; for his mouth speaks from that which fills his heart.

  1. We tend to blame other people or our circumstances for our sinful words and behaviors. This is especially true with bitterness.

    1. Dr Paul Tripp states, “Christ calls us to humbly accept responsibility for our behavior. He calls us to humbly admit that relationships and circumstances are only the occasions in which our hearts reveal themselves.”9

  2. When a person is displaying the fruits of bitterness, they are revealing their own heart Matthew 15:17-20.

    1. A failure, or resistance, to forgive reveals a heart that is proud and arrogant. Furthermore, it reveals their lack of understanding of how much they have been forgiven by Jesus Christ Matthew 18:23-35.

nestedSubsections.title: How do we Begin Dealing with Bitterness in a Marriage?
nestedSubsections.content: 1. The first step in dealing with bitterness is to forgive your spouse for every sin they have committed against you.

nestedSubsections.title: What is Biblical Forgiveness?
nestedSubsections.content:
1. Dr Jay Adams teaches, “Forgiveness is a lifting of the charge of guilt from another, a formal declaration of that fact and a promise (made and kept) ever to remember the wrong against him in the future.”10
    Hebrews 8:12 For I will be merciful to their iniquities, and I will remember their sins no more.

  2. When a person forgives and no longer “remembers” the incident, it does not mean they will forget it; rather, it means:

    1. They will not dwell on it.

    2. They will not talk about it to others.

    3. They will not bring it up in future conflicts to use against their spouse.

    4. Once the offense is forgiven, the incident is not to stand in the way of reconciliation Matthew 5:23-24.
      Psalms 103:12 As far as the east is from the west, So far has He removed your transgressions from us.

  3. Forgiveness is not a feeling, but an act of the will.

    1. Since forgiveness is not a feeling, we do not wait until we “feel” like forgiving in order to forgive. We must not wait! Forgiveness is to be granted when a person repents because God commands us to forgive.
      Colossians 3:13 You must make allowance for each other’s faults and forgive the person who offends you. Remember, the Lord forgave you, so you must forgive others.

  4. The proper way to seek forgiveness.

    1. The proper way to seek forgiveness from someone you have sinned against is to confess your sin and ask for forgiveness.

    2. Simply saying “I’m sorry” does not resolve conflicts.

nestedSubsections.title: Hindrances to Overcoming Bitterness:
nestedSubsections.content:
1. Blindness (Being Unaware of Bitterness)

    1. Due to the subtle way that bitterness overtakes the heart, a person can literally be blind to even having it.

  2. The Victim Mentality

    1. Someone who has been wronged will often struggle to recognize and admit that their bitterness has contributed to the problem.

  3. Pride

    1. It may be difficult to seek forgiveness for bitterness, especially when they were wronged.

      1. They need to actively seek forgiveness for the bitterness that was harbored in their heart.

  4. Habit

    1. A bitter person habitually becomes harsh and cold, often using cruel tones, mean words, and giving the cold shoulder.

  5. Lack of Trust

    1. Trust may have been seriously damaged by false repentance and repeated wrongdoings.

      1. The inability to trust is understandable after a long, chronically hurtful relationship, but it gets in the way of overcoming bitterness.

  6. Fear

    1. There is fear of an insincere repentance and of being hurt again.

  7. Animosity

    1. It is difficult, truly an act of the will, to give affection to someone that you’ve built up hateful feelings toward.

nestedSubsections.title: A. To destroy bitterness: Stop taking into account the wrongs you’ve suffered
nestedSubsections.content:
1. A. To destroy bitterness:

    1. Stop taking into account the wrongs you’ve suffered 1 Corinthians 13:5.

      1. This is accomplished through earnest and sincere forgiveness.

    2. Acknowledge the bitterness that has taken root in their heart and seek forgiveness for it.

    3. Remove all of the hindrances to overcoming bitterness through humility, trusting God, prayer, and taking action!

      1. Put off bitterness and put on love Ephesians 4:22-32.

      2. Martha Peace suggests making “second mile investments” which is “doing something extra special nice” for your spouse. Peace reminds us that, “It is never easy to go against your feelings and go the ‘second mile, but it is a necessary step towards overcoming bitterness” Matthew 5:41. 11

    4. Begin putting on gratitude and contentment.

      1. If we are thankful for our spouse, it is hard to be discontent and bitter against them.
        Philippians 4:11 Not that I speak from want, for I have learned to be content in whatever circumstances I am.

nestedSubsections.title: Summary:
nestedSubsections.content:
1. Bitterness occurs when a person takes into account a wrong suffered. They fail to forgive and file away how they have been wronged. Over time they become cruel and harsh with their words, they take up evil actions against their spouse. This eventually becomes a habit.

  2. To overcome it they must see bitterness as a sinful response to their situation. The embittered spouse must forgive their spouse for the wrongs he has done against her, and she must also seek forgiveness for her bitterness from both God and her husband.

  3. Furthermore, to overcome bitterness one must practice putting off the cruel words and tones and evil actions and put on kind words and actions. Indeed, it is important to go the extra mile and do extra special kind deeds and speak extra special kind words. This is called the “second mile” principle. Going the extra mile habitually will renew love in relationships and be pleasing to God.

  1. Stuart Scott, The Exemplary Husband: A Biblical Perspective, 201.

  2. Martha Peace, The Excellent Wife: A Biblical Perspective, 92.

  3. Jerry Bridges, Respectable Sin: Confronting the Sins We Tolerate, 160.

  4. Jerry Bridges, Respectable Sin: Confronting the Sins We Tolerate, 161.

  5. Martha Peace, The Excellent Wife: A Biblical Perspective, 88.

  6. Martha Peace, The Excellent Wife: A Biblical Perspective, 92.

  7. Emery and Brewster, The New Century Dictionary of the English Language, 174.

  8. Martha Peace, The Excellent Wife: A Biblical Perspective, 89.

  9. Paul David Tripp, Instruments in the Redeemer’s Hands: People in Need of Change Helping People in Need of Change, 62.

  10. Jay E. Adams, A Theology of Christian Counseling, 229.

  11. Martha Peace, The Excellent Wife: A Biblical Perspective, 93.

subsections.title: Homework Questions
subsections.content: Complete the exercises below and save your answers.

questions.question: Discuss this lesson with your spouse and make sure you both understand it well.
Examine your heart to see if you are keeping a ledger of sins against your spouse. If there is, take the steps necessary to destroy this ledger!

Examine your heart to see if there are sins you have committed against your spouse, which are unresolved. If there are, go and confess your sin and seek forgiveness. Also, confess your sin to God and ask for forgiveness.
Examine your heart to see if you have become bitter. Do you exhibit any of the signs or symptoms of bitterness?
Put the “second mile” principle into effect. Start doing at least one “second mile” action for your spouse each day.

Application

  • Let your motivation to forgive and overcome bitterness be a desire to be pleasing to God. 2 Corinthians 5:15.
